title: From pharmacy technician to pharmacy operations manager, the career ladder explained with Ledger in 90 seconds
summary: A healthcare job viewers meet at the counter; the ladder shows the support rungs around the pharmacist. Weakest sourced of the seven, so replace it if Hoang prefers.

beats.voice: From pharmacy technician to pharmacy operations manager, the career ladder explained with Ledger in ninety seconds.
onScreen: From pharmacy technician to pharmacy operations manager, the career ladder explained with Ledger
beats.visual: Title scene: full-bleed room, a ladder on the right, the five steps below, small Ledger in the ph_tech outfit waving on the bottom step; a dashed arrow climbs to the top; the title card and the 90-second pill appear on the title words

beats.label: rung 1 PHARMACY TECH
beats.voice: First, Ledger is the pharmacy technician, in scrubs.
beats.visual: OUTFIT (ph_tech: pale-green scrub top, white lab coat unbuttoned, name tag, hair cap not used). Header PHARMACY TECH. Ledger alone, scale 3.2; arrows pop in on 'scrubs' and 'name tag'; pharmacy shelves behind

beats.label: rung 1 PHARMACY TECH
beats.voice: Then he labels each prescription, and logs it.
beats.visual: Tablets count into a bottle; a label prints; a screen logs it

beats.label: rung 1 PHARMACY TECH
beats.voice: He passes each one to the pharmacist, who checks it.
beats.visual: A bag slides to a pharmacist figure who stamps it

beats.label: rung 1 PHARMACY TECH
beats.voice: So on this rung, he fills every prescription himself.
beats.visual: Slider at 0.06 on 'Fills'

beats.label: climb 1 to 2
beats.voice: After that, he climbs to lead technician.
beats.visual: Ledger climbs the ladder from rung 1 to rung 2; his outfit swaps mid-climb to the next set; the next rung tag lights up on the naming word

beats.label: rung 2 LEAD TECHNICIAN
beats.voice: Now he leads the other technicians, and trains the new ones.
beats.visual: OUTFIT (ph_lead: white lab coat over teal scrubs, lanyard, pen, clipboard). Header LEAD TECHNICIAN. Two technician figures follow him along the shelves

beats.label: rung 2 LEAD TECHNICIAN
beats.voice: Then he tracks stock, and alerts the pharmacist to shortages.
beats.visual: A stock meter drops into red; a note goes to the pharmacist

beats.label: rung 2 LEAD TECHNICIAN
beats.voice: So he fills a little less, and starts to direct.
beats.visual: Slider at 0.3

beats.label: climb 2 to 3
beats.voice: Then he climbs again, to technician specialist.
beats.visual: Ledger climbs the ladder from rung 2 to rung 3; his outfit swaps mid-climb to the next set; the next rung tag lights up on the naming word

beats.label: rung 3 TECH SPECIALIST
beats.voice: As specialist, he handles insurance claims and prior approvals.
beats.visual: OUTFIT (ph_specialist: dark-blue scrubs, glasses, headset, laptop). Header TECH SPECIALIST. A claim form gets a green tick on a laptop

beats.label: rung 3 TECH SPECIALIST
beats.voice: He also calls doctors' offices, to confirm each dose.
beats.visual: A phone shows a doctor's office; a dose is ticked

beats.label: rung 3 TECH SPECIALIST
beats.voice: And he plans the schedule.
beats.visual: A weekly schedule grid fills

beats.label: climb 3 to 4
beats.voice: Next, he steps up as assistant manager.
beats.visual: Ledger climbs the ladder from rung 3 to rung 4; his outfit swaps mid-climb to the next set; the next rung tag lights up on the naming word

beats.label: rung 4 ASSISTANT MANAGER
beats.voice: Now he helps manage the pharmacy, and oversees a larger team.
beats.visual: OUTFIT (ph_assistant: navy blazer over scrubs top, lanyard, tablet). Header ASSISTANT MANAGER. Org chart with six small figures below Ledger

beats.label: rung 4 ASSISTANT MANAGER
beats.voice: Then he covers for the manager, and handles the staff rota.
beats.visual: He sits at the manager's desk; a rota fills

beats.label: climb 4 to 5
beats.voice: Finally, he reaches the top rung, as operations manager.
beats.visual: Ledger climbs the ladder from rung 4 to rung 5; his outfit swaps mid-climb to the next set; the next rung tag lights up on the naming word

beats.label: rung 5 OPS MANAGER
beats.voice: Finally, as operations manager, he runs the pharmacy's daily work.
beats.visual: OUTFIT (ph_manager: dark suit with a white coat over it, glasses, grey temples, gold pin). Header OPS MANAGER. Full pharmacy cutaway with counter, shelves and back room

beats.label: rung 5 OPS MANAGER
beats.voice: He sets the staffing and the budget, while pharmacists check each prescription.
beats.visual: A staffing board and a budget meter; pharmacists stamp at a counter

beats.label: rung 5 OPS MANAGER
beats.voice: Yet he fills almost nothing himself, and answers for the whole pharmacy.
beats.visual: Slider at 0.95 on 'Directs'; every counter has a tick

beats.label: payoff
beats.voice: So with each rung, Ledger filled less, and directed more.
beats.visual: Five Ledgers on the ladder, all five tags ticked, the slider runs from the bottom word to the top word

caption:
From pharmacy technician to operations manager, the job changes on every rung

The pharmacy technician labels each prescription, and the lead technician trains the team and tracks the stock. Then the assistant manager covers for the manager. Finally, the operations manager runs the pharmacy's daily work, while pharmacists check each prescription

So each rung up, you fill fewer prescriptions yourself and direct more of the pharmacy. Walk up the ladder with Ledger and note which rung you are on

openQuestions: Weakest ladder: the sources describe the technician, lead and specialist rungs but none names a 'pharmacy operations manager'. The Pharmacy Times article is one person's career, the BLS says only that technicians may take supervisory roles, and the National Careers Service says 'lead pharmacy technician or department manager'. In many countries the pharmacy manager is a pharmacist, so 'operations manager' avoids that claim. Recommend swapping this slot for another ladder from the backlog unless Hoang accepts it.
Pharmacy Times says the example technician 'oversaw 16 employees'; the script states no number.
Titles vary by employer and country; the caption says nothing about pay or years
